sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: The Puerto Rican royal palm is a solitary palm native to Hispaniola, Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands. It commonly reaches 12–18 m and can exceed 26 m; its smooth stem is about 25–70 cm in diameter.

sections.title: Crown and fruit
sections.text: Large pinnate leaves form a crown above a long green crownshaft. Branched inflorescences carry small flowers followed by oval, dark-purple fruits. The plate accurately shows the ringed stem, crown, inflorescences and fruit.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: It is widely planted as an ornamental. Ethnobotanical sources report use of the palm heart, the terminal bud; harvesting it kills the stem. Birds feed on the fruits, but the sources consulted do not document them as human food.
